## Summary

Fixes incorrect file path references in AI workflow documentation that were causing cascading tool errors in AI assistant sessions.

## Root Cause

Three documentation files contained wrong file paths that don't match actual files on disk:

1. **`.ai-workflows/folder-structure.md`** — referenced `includes/core.php`, `includes/plugin.php`, `includes/updater.php` (lowercase) but actual files use PascalCase: `includes/Core.php`, `includes/Plugin.php`, `includes/Updater.php`

2. **`.ai-workflows/bug-fixing.md`** — referenced `fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices.php` and `languages/fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices.pot` (missing `wp-` prefix) instead of the correct `wp-fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices.php` and `languages/wp-fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices.pot`

3. **`.ai-workflows/feature-development.md`** — referenced `reference-plugins/` directory that does not exist in the repository

Incorrect paths in documentation cause AI assistants to:
1. Try to read non-existent paths — `read:file_not_found` (23x observed)

3. Read stale/wrong file then edit different target — `edit:edit_stale_read` (32x observed)

- `.ai-workflows/bug-fixing.md`: Fix 2 file references in Hotfix section to include `wp-` prefix
- `.ai-workflows/feature-development.md`: Remove reference to non-existent `reference-plugins/` directory

title: GH#18: fix require_once casing to match PascalCase filenames on disk
body:
## Summary

Fixes fatal errors on case-sensitive Linux file systems caused by lowercase `require_once` paths pointing to PascalCase files on disk.

## Changes

- **`wp-fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices.php:35`** — `includes/plugin.php` → `includes/Plugin.php`
- **`includes/Plugin.php:113`** — `includes/core.php` → `includes/Core.php`
- **`.ai-workflows/folder-structure.md`** — Updated Includes Directory listing, naming convention rule, and @mention references to reflect PascalCase

## Why

On case-insensitive macOS, `require_once 'includes/plugin.php'` succeeds even though the file is `Plugin.php`. On Linux production servers (case-sensitive), this causes a fatal PHP error preventing the plugin from loading. The files on disk were already PascalCase; only the `require_once` paths and documentation were wrong.

## Verification

```bash
grep -n "require_once" wp-fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices.php includes/Plugin.php
grep -n "core.php\|plugin.php\|updater.php" .ai-workflows/folder-structure.md
```

Resolves #18

## Summary

Adds the missing `require_once` for `includes/Updater.php` in the `load_dependencies()` method of `includes/Plugin.php`. The `Updater` class was instantiated in `init_components()` but its file was never explicitly loaded, which would cause a fatal error on any WordPress installation not using an autoloader (there is no PSR-4 autoloader for `includes/` — only an optional Composer autoloader for `vendor/`).

Also fixes the case mismatch: `includes/core.php` → `includes/Core.php` to match the actual filename, which would silently fail on Linux (case-sensitive) servers.

- **EDIT**: `includes/Plugin.php:113` — changed `includes/core.php` to `includes/Core.php`

title: GH#25: implement PSR-4 autoloader, remove manual require_once
body:
## Summary

Implements a PSR-4 autoloader using `spl_autoload_register` in the `Plugin` class, eliminating manual `require_once` calls for each class file. New classes under either the root namespace (`includes/`) or the `Admin` sub-namespace (`admin/lib/`) are now loaded automatically.

## Changes

- `includes/Plugin.php`: Added `register_autoloader()` method registered in the constructor. Maps namespace prefixes to directories; removed manual `require_once` calls.
- `admin/lib/admin.php` renamed to `Admin.php`: PSR-4 requires filename to match class name (case-sensitive on Linux).
- `admin/lib/modal.php` renamed to `Modal.php`: Same reason.
- `composer.json`: Fixed namespace case (`WPAllStars` to `WPALLSTARS`) and added `admin/lib/` mapping for `Admin\` sub-namespace.
- `wp-fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices.php`: Fixed `require_once` path to use `Plugin.php` (capital P).

## Verification

The Composer vendor autoloader (when present) takes precedence; the custom autoloader always acts as a fallback. No behavioural change — the same classes are loaded in the same order via the autoloader stack instead of explicit file paths.

Resolves #25

title: GH#29: fix autoloader precedence and optimise PSR-4 namespace lookup
body:
## What was done

Both findings from the Gemini code review of PR #27 have been addressed in `includes/Plugin.php`.

**Finding 1 — Composer autoloader precedence (line 80)**

The constructor previously called `register_autoloader()` before `load_dependencies()`. Since `spl_autoload_register` appends to the stack, the custom PSR-4 loader was position 1 (tried first) and Composer position 2, inverting the intended priority. The two calls are now swapped: `load_dependencies()` runs first so Composer is registered at position 1 and the custom loader is the fallback.

**Finding 2 — Autoloader efficiency (line 132)**

Three optimisations applied to the closure inside `register_autoloader()`:
1. Early-exit guard: `strncmp` against the base plugin prefix before entering the loop, so every foreign class (the vast majority of WordPress lookups) returns immediately without touching the map.
2. Static namespace map: the array is now allocated once across all calls via `static $namespace_map = null`, not on every invocation.
3. `require` instead of `require_once`: the autoloader is only invoked for classes not yet defined, so the file-inclusion hash lookup in `require_once` is redundant overhead.

## Testing

- `php -l includes/Plugin.php` — no syntax errors.
- Logic verified: Composer registers first → has higher stack priority; foreign-class lookups return on the `strncmp` guard without iterating; map is allocated once.

Resolves #29

title: GH#46: 3.0.0 small Plugins-screen-only helper, no update meddling
body:
## What

3.0.0 rebuilds the plugin as a small helper that runs only on the Plugins screen. It no longer touches WordPress updates. The owner wants it kept small and lightweight, for this one problem only.

Resolves #46
For #47 (README rewrite done here, but #47 stays open until SEO Pro Stack is public and its link loads without signing in)

## Why the "Remove Notice" link went

The link never worked. On WordPress 6.2 with PHP 7.4, the old plugin added a "(File Missing)" row and a Remove Notice link. But in the same page load, core's `validate_active_plugins()` (plugins.php, after `prepare_items()`) had already switched the plugin off. Clicking the link redirected to `plugins.php?reference_removal_failed=1`. The fake row also logged `PHP Notice: Undefined index: DomainPath`.

## Changes

- `includes/Plugin.php` holds the whole plugin, about 200 lines:
  - On `load-plugins.php`, it lists missing active plugins (site and network, using the same check as core) and cleans `recently_activated` and `uninstall_plugins`.
  - On `pre_current_active_plugins`, it prints a plain explanation below core's message.
  - It has no settings and makes no outside requests. It has no JS or CSS, and it stores nothing. It deletes the old `fpden_update_source` option once.
- Removed:
  - `Core.php`, `Updater.php` and all of `admin/` (the update source chooser, the notice JS and the CSS);
  - the `Update URI` and Gitea headers;
  - the Composer runtime dependency;
  - the plugin details override, which showed made-up ratings and an install count of 1,000;
  - the code that deleted the update caches for every plugin, theme and core, and ran `wp_cache_flush()`, on every visit to the Plugins screen.
- Requires WordPress 6.2 and PHP 7.4.
- `build.sh` builds the zip with rsync and `.distignore`. `release.yml` now uses it and checks that the tag matches `Version:`. It drops the WordPress.org deploy job, because the plugin isn't on WordPress.org.
- Added PHPCS (full WordPress standard plus PHP 7.4 compatibility) and PHPStan level 8, run with `composer lint`.
- Rewrote `README.md` for people searching the error, and `readme.txt` (2.9 KB). Rewrote `AGENTS.md` and regenerated the `.pot`.
- Deleted the AI tool config files, `.wiki` (the GitHub wiki has no content) and `.ai-workflows`.

## Verification

- `composer lint`: PHPCS clean, PHPStan level 8 reports no errors.
- `./build.sh` makes a 15 KB zip with 6 files under `wp-fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices/`.
- WordPress 6.2 with PHP 7.4 (`wordpress:php7.4-apache`), single site:
  - Setup: two active plugins whose folders were deleted, a stale `recently_activated` entry and a stale `uninstall_plugins` entry.
  - First Plugins load: core's message appears, then our notice lists both plugins and says "Removed 2 leftover entries". Both options are cleaned and `fpden_update_source` is deleted.
  - Second load: no notice. `debug.log` is empty.
